metadata.description: Hostile input corpus for status line sanitiser testing. Uses real JSON unicode escapes: \u001b=ESC, \u0007=BEL, \n=LF, etc. json.load() yields true bytes/characters.
metadata.sanitiser_rule: Strip all disallowed characters and sequences in place; preserve surrounding printable text; do NOT truncate.
metadata.rule: strip disallowed characters and escape sequences in place, preserving all surrounding printable text; never truncate. HT (0x09) is replaced by a single space; every other stripped element is removed with no replacement.
metadata.encoding: All control characters are encoded as standard JSON \u escapes, so json.load() with default strict=True yields the true hostile string. Each case carries raw_len = len(raw) after decoding, as a self-check against re-encoding accidents.

test_cases.description: OSC-8 hyperlink with ST (String Terminator) = ESC backslash
test_cases.threat: Terminal creates clickable link to attacker URL; user may accidentally click
test_cases.notes: ST terminator is ESC (0x1B) followed by backslash (0x5C)

test_cases.description: OSC-8 hyperlink with BEL (0x07) terminator
test_cases.threat: Same as above; some terminals prefer BEL over ST
test_cases.notes: BEL (0x07) is the older terminator for OSC sequences; still recognized by modern terminals

test_cases.description: OSC-8 with parameter and ST terminator
test_cases.threat: Full-featured hyperlink with session tracking; more sophisticated attack
test_cases.notes: id=mysession is an OSC-8 parameter that allows tracking; still a full OSC sequence

test_cases.description: OSC-0 (Set window title) with BEL terminator
test_cases.threat: Changes terminal/window title to misleading text; may trick user into thinking they are in a different context
test_cases.notes: OSC-0 is commonly used; many terminals honor it

test_cases.description: OSC-2 (Set both icon name and window title in xterm)
test_cases.threat: Window title spoofing
test_cases.notes: Less widely supported than OSC-0 but still a vector

test_cases.description: OSC-52 clipboard write with base64 data (decodes to 'check again later')
test_cases.threat: CRITICAL: Silently writes to clipboard without user knowledge; decoded data could be a malicious command, SSH key, or credential.
test_cases.notes: OSC-52 is supported by xterm, tmux, and many modern terminals; allows arbitrary clipboard write

test_cases.description: CSI cursor movement: up 5 lines (CUU), left 10 columns (CUB), then 'malicious'
test_cases.threat: Overwrites previous status line output or adjacent text above
test_cases.notes: CSI sequences: ESC[<n>A (CUU up), ESC[<n>B (CUD down), ESC[<n>C (CUF right), ESC[<n>D (CUB left). Strip sequences in place; preserve text.

test_cases.description: CSI erase entire line (EL 2K)
test_cases.threat: Clears the status line from terminal display
test_cases.notes: EL (Erase in Line): ESC[0K (erase to EOL), ESC[1K (erase from BOL), ESC[2K (erase entire line)

test_cases.description: CSI erase display (ED 2J)
test_cases.threat: Clears entire screen; severely disorienting
test_cases.notes: ED (Erase in Display): ESC[0J (below), ESC[1J (above), ESC[2J (entire)

test_cases.description: DECSTBM set scrolling region (lines 2-10)
test_cases.threat: Constrains terminal scrolling; disorienting, may hide output
test_cases.notes: Private CSI DECSTBM: ESC[<top>;<bottom>r

test_cases.description: DECSET mode 1049: use alternate screen buffer
test_cases.threat: Switches to alternate buffer, hiding content; may confuse user or cause display corruption
test_cases.notes: Private mode DECSET: ESC[?<num>h (set), ESC[?<num>l (reset). Mode 1049 is alternate screen buffer

test_cases.description: DECSET mode 1000: enable mouse reporting
test_cases.threat: Enables mouse tracking; while not immediately dangerous to output, unexpected in a status line context
test_cases.notes: Mode 1000 enables X11 mouse reporting; mode 1002 enables drag reporting

test_cases.description: Bare newline (0x0A) in repo name
test_cases.threat: CRITICAL: breaks the status line's guaranteed 2-line contract; makes output unreadable and corrupts the banner layout
test_cases.notes: Strip the newline character; keep surrounding text. Do not truncate.

test_cases.description: Carriage return (0x0D); moves cursor to start of line
test_cases.threat: Overwrites beginning of the status line; causes display corruption
test_cases.notes: CR without LF; moves cursor but does not advance line. Strip in place.

test_cases.description: Multiple backspaces (0x08) to overwrite 'repo' with 'MAL'
test_cases.threat: Corrupts visible output; user sees 'MAL' instead of intended text
test_cases.notes: Backspace is 0x08; terminal moves cursor left without erasing. Strip backspaces; keep text.

test_cases.description: Embedded null byte (0x00) between 'my' and 'repo'
test_cases.threat: May truncate string in C-style processing; breaks string length assumptions in visible_len()
test_cases.notes: NUL is 0x00; typically terminates strings in C/C++. Strip in place.

test_cases.description: Bare ESC (0x1B) without a following sequence (no bracket, no OSC introducer)
test_cases.threat: Dangling escape; terminal state undefined; may interpret next character as sequence start; corrupts next output
test_cases.notes: A lone ESC is incomplete and dangerous; should never reach terminal output. Strip in place.

test_cases.description: Bell/alert character (0x07) not part of an OSC sequence
test_cases.threat: Produces audible alert; may trigger other behaviors in some terminals
test_cases.notes: BEL (0x07) is historically used as OSC terminator but also a bare alert character. Strip when standalone.

test_cases.description: Tab character (0x09)
test_cases.threat: Tabs advance to next tab stop; unpredictable width in terminal; breaks width accounting and background fill
test_cases.notes: Tab (HT, 0x09) must be replaced with a space, not allowed as-is. Width accounting assumes printable chars only.

test_cases.description: 8-bit CSI (0x9B) instead of ESC [ (equivalent to ESC [ 31m = red)
test_cases.threat: Modern UTF-8 terminals may still recognize 8-bit C1 control codes; enables color injection
test_cases.notes: 0x9B is the 8-bit equivalent of ESC[; UTF-8 encoding of 0x9B is C2 9B; strip in place

test_cases.description: 8-bit OSC (0x9D) instead of ESC ] (equivalent to ESC ] 8...)
test_cases.threat: May be recognized by terminals; enables OSC sequence injection
test_cases.notes: 0x9D is the 8-bit equivalent of ESC]; UTF-8 encoding is C2 9D. Strip the full OSC sequence.

test_cases.description: String ends with incomplete ESC (0x1B), no following bracket or OSC introducer
test_cases.threat: Dangling escape leaves terminal in unexpected state for next output; corrupts subsequent status line renders
test_cases.notes: A naive regex that only strips complete sequences (e.g., \u001b\[[0-9;]*m) will leave a dangling ESC behind. Must strip incomplete.

test_cases.description: Incomplete CSI: ESC [ 3 (waiting for more digits or terminating letter)
test_cases.threat: Dangling CSI prefix; next character may be misinterpreted as part of the sequence
test_cases.notes: CSI syntax is ESC [ <param> <param> ... <letter>; ending early is dangerous. Strip incomplete sequences.

test_cases.description: Incomplete OSC: ESC ] 8 (waiting for semicolon and URL)
test_cases.threat: Terminal enters OSC-parsing state; next character may be misinterpreted
test_cases.notes: OSC syntax is ESC ] <number> ; <data> <terminator>; incomplete sequences are dangerous. Strip.

test_cases.description: Repo name with emoji (rocket: U+1F680)
test_cases.threat: NONE
test_cases.notes: Legitimate content that MUST SURVIVE unchanged; emoji are valid in repo names on many filesystems; test for false positives

test_cases.description: Repo name starting with Chinese characters (U+4E2D U+6587 = 'Chinese' 中文)
test_cases.threat: NONE
test_cases.notes: CJK characters are double-width; must preserve for visible_len() calculation. Test for false positives.

test_cases.description: Latin 'cafe' + combining acute accent (U+0301) = 'café' in combining form (not precomposed)
test_cases.threat: NONE
test_cases.notes: Combining marks (category Mn) have zero width; must survive; visible_len() uses unicodedata.combining(). Test for false positives.

test_cases.description: English 'repo-' + Arabic (U+0645 U+0631 U+062D U+0628 U+0627 = 'marhaba' مرحبا, right-to-left)
test_cases.threat: NONE
test_cases.notes: RTL text is valid and intentional; must survive; terminal handles bidirectional display. Test for false positives.

test_cases.description: Left-to-Right Override (U+202D) + 'malicious' + Pop Directional Formatting (U+202C)
test_cases.threat: Spoofing via bidirectional text manipulation: can make 'repo' appear to be followed by RTL text, or hide text by reversing its visual order. No escape sequences, but a display deception.
test_cases.notes: U+202D (LRO), U+202E (RLO), U+202C (PDF) are bidi overrides. RFC 9591 suggests stripping for security. Strip in place.

test_cases.description: Zero-width joiner (U+200D) between 'my' and 'repo'
test_cases.threat: MINIMAL; may affect ligature joining in some scripts; typically not a display spoofing vector
test_cases.notes: Zero-width joiners are used legitimately in emoji sequences and Indic/Arabic ligatures. ALLOW; do not strip.

test_cases.description: Zero-width non-joiner (U+200C)
test_cases.threat: MINIMAL; used to prevent ligatures in some scripts; not a display spoofing vector
test_cases.notes: U+200C is safe; used legitimately in Persian, Arabic, and other scripts. ALLOW; do not strip.

test_cases.description: Word joiner (U+2060)
test_cases.threat: MINIMAL; prevents line breaking; not a spoofing vector
test_cases.notes: U+2060 is safe; legitimate use in preventing line breaks. ALLOW; do not strip.

test_cases.description: OSC-8 (BEL terminator) + CSI red (31m) + CSI reset (0m) all in one string
test_cases.threat: Multiple attack vectors chained; corrupts output in multiple ways (hyperlink + color injection)
test_cases.notes: Sanitiser must handle all sequences in a single pass; cannot assume one sequence per string. Strip all in place.

test_cases.description: Normal spaces, then OSC-0, then space, then CSI red
test_cases.threat: Interleaved whitespace and sequences; must not corrupt spaces
test_cases.notes: Space before OSC (1 char) + OSC stripped + space after OSC (1 char) = two spaces total. Preserve all whitespace.

test_cases.description: String containing only escape sequences, no printable text
test_cases.threat: Sanitiser returns empty string; renderer must cope with empty segments
test_cases.notes: A repo name that is only OSC and CSI sequences results in an empty string after sanitising. Renderer must handle gracefully (no stray separator).

test_cases.description: Very long string (1k+ chars) with a dangling ESC at the end
test_cases.threat: Sanitiser must not degrade to quadratic behavior or excessive memory use
test_cases.notes: Dangling ESC stripped; all printable text preserved. Sanitiser should complete in linear time. Test for O(n) behavior, not O(n²) or worse.
